520	He said: cast lots. They cast lots, and the lot fell on Rabban Shimon ben
521	Gamliel.
522	Immediately Rabbi Yishmael was shaken. The other one didn't even have time to be shaken, he grabbed the sword, whack!
523	He took off his head, and it rolled to the head of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.
524	Rabbi Yishmael picked up that head and began to cry out.
525	He said: This is the Nasi of Israel, look what happened to him.
526	This is the holy one of Israel. He kissed that face and said: Could such a tongue have spoken Torah?
527	"This is the Torah, and this is its reward?" A heavenly voice came out and said:
528	Be silent, Rabbi Yishmael. If you cry out one more time, I will destroy the world.
529	And Rabbi Yishmael fell silent.
530	See what this is, how much pain he felt.
531	Then the executioner came, it is written there, to seize Rabbi Yishmael.
532	First of all, how did Rabbi Yishmael become impure to...
533	Rabbi Yishmael was a Kohen Gadol. If he was a Kohen, how could a Kohen become impure to a corpse?
534	It is forbidden to become impure to a corpse.
535	So that is what is meant: a met mitzvah.
536	And some say it wasn't under a roof, it was under the open sky, but that is also a stretch.
537	What?
538	Tzaddikim don't coordinate. So what, didn't you read Responsa Maase Merkavot, part 1, section 11?
539	You didn't read it?
540	What, part 1 came out 15 years ago, and you still haven't read it?
541	Wow, so what do you read on Shabbat?
542	No, what do you read, newspapers?
543	No, the newspapers here?
544	There are newspapers here from all sorts of regions, huh?
545	Where, where, where, flyers?
546	All the flyers, you should know how they rehash all the stories.
547	One steals the jokes from the other, one steals the stories from the other.
548	Everything has already gone around and come back again and again, baruch HaShem, Shaar HaGilgulim.
549	What?
550	I think so.
551	Yes, you think so, yes.
552	That our Yosef, he forgave them, only everyone is truly upon them.
553	That's what I think.
554	Okay, good that you think.
555	Keep thinking.
556	Think.
557	It's good to think.
558	How can it be that he didn't forgive them?
559	I don't know, maybe he forgave, but he needed to say it out loud: "I forgive."
